![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14111253/assets/4d83f771aa650879909c33d7033e80ca044b7e6f8369e19667e6173aa8a40737.png)

Evaluate ${\int }_{C}(x+\sqrt{3y})\,\text{d}y,$ where $C$ is the path traversed along the line segment from the point $(2,0)$ to the point $(0,3),$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

The curve $C$ is a line segment with endpoints $(2,0)$ and $(0,3).$ It can be parametrized as 

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨(2+t(0-2)),\,(0+t(3-0))⟩ \\  & =⟨2-2t,\,3t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$

Computing $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)=3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=x+\sqrt{3y}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =(2-2t)+\sqrt{3(3t)} \\  & =2-2t+3\sqrt{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2-2t+3\sqrt{t})\cdot 3\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}(2-2t+3{t}^{1/2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =3{[2t-{t}^{2}+2{t}^{3/2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3[(2(1)-(1)^{2}+2(1)^{3/2})-(0)] \\  & =3(3) \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$
